title: A v0 length off-by-one in the Solidity commit-path encoder changes no M0 outcome
reproduction: Mutation NM0_1 (sol_v0_len_off_by_one) in a scratch copy of facts/morph_header.json: enc_sol(h v0) stays 249 bytes long, but ok_sol(enc_sol(h)) becomes False. Running `holon run --facts <copy> --no-registry` moves no law's status (scratchpad/audit_i5 (session scratch, not committed), mut/log.txt).
suggested_fix: Add a round-trip law over the Solidity side: ok_sol(enc_sol(h)) for every version.

title: A Go v1 validator that accepts len >= 257 changes no M0 outcome
reproduction: Mutation NM0_3 (go_v1_len_ge): ok_go(258-byte v1 header) becomes True instead of False. No law moves (mut/log.txt).
suggested_fix: Add a PAR-domain law for version 1 (the analogue of L_dom_hdr), or a family over all versions.

title: revertBatch keeping the revert request index changes no M1 outcome
reproduction: Mutation NM1_1 (revert_keeps_rri): trace commitBatch, challengeState, wait, proveState, revertBatch, commitState. The last step goes from ok to 'rev 2 (pending revert request)' on the model, yet no law moves (mut/live_out.txt, mut/log.txt).
suggested_fix: An UNDO law for revertBatch's request-index residue, or an invariant over rri.

title: challengeState without its in-challenge guard changes no M1 outcome
reproduction: Mutation NM1_2 (challenge_no_inch_guard): a second challengeState now succeeds instead of reverting with 'already in challenge'. No law moves (mut/live_out.txt, mut/log.txt).
suggested_fix: A SYM or DISCH law about concurrent challenges (at most one open).

title: A consistently forged replay outcome passes the full gate (G6 cannot rerun the real code)
reproduction: Attack B: forge L_fact_Z's go_consumer outcome in replay/M1/report.json consistently (outcomes, classes, flags), then `holon run --milestone M1` and the full gate in a copy: GATE PASSED (scratchpad/audit_i5 (session scratch, not committed), attackB_M1_gate.json). This is the known limit stated in docs/iterations/I4.md: G6 checks consistency, not re-execution.
suggested_fix: Re-execute `holon replay` on a trusted runner (CI) and compare the report byte for byte; until then, label replay reports as agent-writable evidence.

title: A counter-law proved at a witness other than the recorded (replayed) one passes the gate
reproduction: Attack C: in a copy, the counter-law PROOF.bend proves the refutation at a witness different from record.witness (the one the replay binds by hash); the full gate passed (scratchpad/audit_i5 (session scratch, not committed), attackC_M0_gate.json). The law stays refuted (the kernel-checked witness is genuine), but the replayed witness is not tied to the kernel-checked one. Detailed reproduction was in the stopped audit session.
suggested_fix: G1/G5: regenerate the counter-law PROOF.bend from record.witness and require it byte-identical (or parse the witness constants out of the checked file).

title: An unreachable constructed inhabitant recorded as reachable passes the gate
reproduction: Attack D: in a copy, a non-vacuity witness built as a constructed state (not run(p, s0)) is recorded with reachable: true; the full gate passed (scratchpad/audit_i5 (session scratch, not committed), attackD_M1_gate.json). Non-vacuity itself still holds (the inhabitant checks); what is overstated is reachability.
suggested_fix: G11V: recompute `reachable` from the witness shape (every state binder is {run: ...} from s0) instead of trusting the field.

title: No check ties a record's artifacts.proof to its artifacts.laws (co-location)
reproduction: Attack A (both milestones): the gate passed after the co-location edit (scratchpad/audit_i5 (session scratch, not committed), attackA_M0_gate.json, attackA_M1_gate.json). holon/ is not frozen (Q1), so regeneration-based checks trust the generators.
suggested_fix: G11: require artifacts.proof and artifacts.laws to be siblings under gen/<m>/<law>/ and PROOF.bend to import exactly that LAWS.bend.
